action.description: The operation to run (one enum value). Every other parameter belongs to one or more actions and is named in its description

timestep.description: Physics timestep in seconds (create_world default, set_timestep): a finite positive float, e.g. 0.002

gravity.description: Gravity vector [x, y, z] in m/s^2 (create_world, set_gravity); default [0, 0, -9.81]

ground_plane.description: create_world: add a flat ground plane (default true); false for a free-floating scene

terrain.description: create_world: heightfield terrain kind ('rough' = bumps, 'stairs' = step plateaus along +x, 'pyramid' = concentric step plateaus toward the centre, 'slope' = constant-grade incline); omit for a flat ground plane. MuJoCo backend only.

difficulty.description: create_world: terrain curriculum knob - scales the heightfield's peak elevation (1.0 = full height, <1 gentler, >1 harsher) to ramp terrain magnitude across resets without changing the terrain kind. Only meaningful together with 'terrain'; difficulty != 1.0 with no terrain is rejected. MuJoCo backend only.

urdf_path.description: Path to a URDF or MJCF file (add_robot for an unregistered robot, register_urdf)

robot_name.description: Which robot the action targets, as listed by list_robots; may be omitted when exactly one robot is loaded

data_config.description: Robot model registry key for add_robot (e.g. 'so101', 'panda', 'aloha'). Use the BARE name from list_urdfs -- not 'so101_default'/'so101_sim' (those are auto-stripped but the bare key is canonical). Auto-resolves to the MJCF/URDF on disk.

keyframe.description: Optional add_robot spawn pose: the name of a <keyframe> in the robot's source model (e.g. 'home' for panda/ur5e/fr3, 'neutral_pose' for aloha) to spawn in that canonical configuration instead of all-zeros. The keyframe's actuator command is applied with the pose, so a gravity-loaded arm holds that configuration instead of sagging out of it; both are restored on reset(). Either the keyframe's name or its integer index in the model is accepted. Omit for the default zero pose; an unknown name errors and lists the available keyframes.

name.description: Instance label. For add_object/add_camera it's the object/camera name. For add_robot it's OPTIONAL -- the label you'll use later in run_policy(robot_name=...); if omitted it's auto-derived from data_config and auto-numbered on collision (so101, so101_2, ...).

position.description: World-frame [x, y, z] in meters: where to place a robot/object/camera, or the move_to end-effector target

orientation.description: Orientation as a unit quaternion in [w, x, y, z] order - scalar first, MuJoCo's convention. Applied verbatim to the body quat, so an [x, y, z, w] vector has the same accepted length and is silently used as a different rotation.

size.description: Vector extent. The convention differs per action and the two are not interchangeable. add_object: FULL extents in meters per axis (not MuJoCo half-extents), as the shape consumes them - box/ellipsoid [x,y,z], cylinder/capsule [diameter,unused,height], sphere [diameter], plane [x] or [x,y] half-widths; mesh ignores it; at most 3 components; a partial vector (e.g. [0.5] for a box) is rejected, not padded - omit size entirely for the 5 cm default. set_geom_properties: the compiled geom's own MuJoCo geom_size components, exactly as many as its type defines and each > 0 - sphere [radius], capsule/cylinder [radius, half-length], box [three half-extents], ellipsoid [three semi-axes], plane [x half-extent, y half-extent, grid spacing]; mesh/height-field/SDF geoms define none, so size is refused for them. The same value therefore means different things: size=[0.2,0.2,0.2] builds a 20 cm box via add_object and resizes that same box to 40 cm via set_geom_properties, and add_object's [diameter,unused,height] capsule triple is refused there (pass [radius, half-length]).

color.description: Colour in 0..1: [r, g, b] (opaque alpha added) or [r, g, b, a]. Any other component count, including an empty list, is rejected - omit color entirely for the default mid-grey.

mass.description: Body mass in kg for add_object (default 0.1). Dynamic objects need a finite value > 0 and >= MuJoCo's mjMINVAL (1e-15); anything else is rejected, since a non-finite mass turns the whole world's state to nan on the next step. Ignored when is_static=true (MuJoCo derives the mass from the geom density).

is_static.description: Fix an add_object body in the world so physics cannot move it. Omit it to leave the choice to the shape: shape='plane' is then made static (a plane is infinite and cannot carry a dynamic mass) and every other shape is dynamic. Sending false for a plane is refused rather than overridden, so omit this rather than spelling out the non-plane default.

mesh_path.description: add_object with shape="mesh": path to the mesh asset (STL/OBJ); required for mesh, ignored otherwise

material.description: Optional visual material/texture for add_object (MuJoCo backend). Keys: reflectance|specular|shininess (float 0..1; specular=0,shininess=0 = matte), texture (absolute image path) OR builtin (checker|gradient|flat) with rgb1/rgb2 ([r,g,b]) + texdim (int, default 512), texrepeat ([u,v]). Omit for a flat color-only surface. Invalid texture path, unknown builtin, empty {}, rgb1/rgb2/texdim without builtin, or any key outside the list above fails loudly (never silently ignored).

target.description: add_camera: world point [x, y, z] the camera looks at

parent_body.description: Optional body name to mount the camera ON (e.g. 'so101/gripper' for a wrist cam). When set, position/target are in that body's LOCAL frame and the camera tracks the body as it moves. Empty/omitted = world-fixed camera.

fov.description: add_camera: vertical field of view in degrees (default 60)

width.description: Image width in pixels (add_camera default 640; render/render_depth/get_world_point default to the camera's own resolution)

height.description: Image height in pixels (add_camera default 480; render/render_depth/get_world_point default to the camera's own resolution)

policy_provider.description: Policy provider name (e.g. groot, lerobot_local, lerobot_async, cosmos3, mock). See list_providers().

instruction.description: Natural-language task text passed to the policy (run_policy, start_policy, eval_policy, evaluate_benchmark)

duration.description: run_policy/start_policy: wall-clock seconds to run the policy (default 10); n_steps takes precedence when given

action_horizon.description: Policy actions consumed from each predicted chunk before re-querying the policy (default 8)

control_frequency.description: Policy control rate in Hz (default 50); sets the physics substeps executed per action

camera_name.description: Camera to render from (render, render_depth, get_world_point): one added via add_camera, or "default"

pixels.description: get_world_point: pixel coordinates [[u, v], ...] to ground to world xyz (u = column from the left, v = row from the top; integer-valued, within the rendered resolution). Pick pixels ON the visible surface of the target (avoid rims/edges/reflections/background) and sample several on the same surface - the returned 'point' is the median over the valid samples; pixels with no depth are dropped (see n_valid). Re-localize after any robot/camera/object motion.

n_steps.description: Number of physics steps to advance (step, default 1; 0 is a no-op) or to run a policy for (run_policy/start_policy, overrides duration). set_gripper uses `steps` for its hold ticks

output_path.description: Destination file path. render: PNG still, confined to the render sandbox (~/.strands_robots/renders, or STRANDS_ROBOTS_RENDER_ROOT); a bare filename like 'frame.png' is written INTO that sandbox, so the sandbox path never has to be spelled out; set STRANDS_ROBOTS_RENDER_ALLOW_ABS=1 to write outside it. export_xml: MJCF scene, any absolute path accepted. run_policy/start_policy/eval_policy/evaluate_benchmark: rollout MP4. Every sink rejects '..' traversal, a symlinked target, backslash separators and shell metacharacters.

fps.description: Frames per second: video rate for run_policy record_video, dataset rate for start_recording. Must be a positive whole number.

randomize_colors.description: randomize: re-sample every non-ground geom's color (default true)

randomize_lighting.description: randomize: jitter light positions (within 0.5 m of authored) and diffuse color (default true)

randomize_physics.description: randomize: scale geom friction and body mass/inertia (default false)

randomize_positions.description: randomize: add uniform xyz noise to dynamic objects, up to position_noise (default false)

position_noise.description: randomize: max +/- xyz offset in meters when randomize_positions is true (default 0.02)

seed.description: Non-negative integer seed for a reproducible random stream (randomize, set_obs_noise, policy runs); omit for fresh entropy

joint_pos_std.description: set_obs_noise: std (radians) of Gaussian noise added to joint positions in get_observation and get_robot_state. Zero (the default) disables it. Must be finite and non-negative.

joint_vel_std.description: set_obs_noise: std (rad/s) of Gaussian noise added to per-joint velocities. Zero (the default) disables it. Must be finite and non-negative.

camera_jitter_px.description: set_obs_noise: max pixel shift applied to rendered frames, uniform in [-px, px] per axis. Zero (the default) disables it. Must be finite and non-negative.

push_to_hub.description: Auto-push dataset to HuggingFace Hub on stop_recording

vcodec.description: Video codec for dataset recording (h264, hevc, libsvtav1)

n_episodes.description: Number of rollout episodes (run_policy, eval_policy, evaluate_benchmark; default 1, positive integer); episodes reset between runs

max_steps.description: Max steps per eval episode; for move_to / rotate_wrist: max control ticks before returning a not-reached error

tol.description: move_to / rotate_wrist convergence tolerance: meters for move_to (EE POSITION only - use orientation_tol for the rotation, default 0.01), radians for rotate_wrist (joint angle, default 0.02)

orientation_tol.description: move_to orientation convergence tolerance in RADIANS (default 0.1, about 5.7 deg). Bounds the rotational half of a pose request, which 'tol' (meters) cannot: when 'orientation' is given, move_to converges to within tol meters AND orientation_tol radians and reports both errors. Only valid alongside 'orientation' - passing it for a position-only move is refused, not ignored

state.description: set_gripper set-point: 'open'/'close' drive the gripper actuator(s) to the set-point-range end declared in the robot registry's gripper metadata when present, else the default convention: 'open' = HIGH end, 'close' = LOW end (SO-100/SO-101 jaw closes toward the low end). The range is the actuator ctrlrange, falling back to the driven joint's limits when the MJCF left the ctrlrange unset

steps.description: set_gripper: control ticks to hold the set-point (each tick advances a few physics substeps); default 12

target_yaw.description: rotate_wrist: wrist-yaw joint set-point in radians (must lie within the joint's range)

fast_mode.description: Skip sleep between actions for faster data collection

body_name.description: Body to act on, as listed by list_bodies (apply_force, get_body_state, set_body_properties, get_jacobian, ...)

site_name.description: get_jacobian: compute the Jacobian at this site instead of a body or geom (give exactly one of body_name/site_name/geom_name)

geom_name.description: Geom to act on (set_geom_properties; get_jacobian as an alternative to body_name/site_name). An add_object name is accepted as its geom

friction.description: set_geom_properties only: the geom's three MuJoCo friction coefficients [sliding, torsional, rolling], each finite and >= 0. Pass all three - a partial vector is rejected, not padded, since there is no value to invent for an omitted coefficient. Takes effect on the next step.

force.description: Force vector [fx, fy, fz] in Newtons

torque_vec.description: Torque vector [tx, ty, tz] in N·m

point.description: Point of force application [x, y, z]

origin.description: raycast/multi_raycast: ray start point [x, y, z] in the world frame, meters

directions.description: Multiple ray directions for multi_raycast - one [dx, dy, dz] per ray, at least one. The batch is all-or-nothing: a direction that cannot be cast refuses it, so a rejected ray is never reported as a miss

exclude_body.description: Body ID whose geoms a ray passes through (-1 = exclude nothing); any other value must be a body id the model defines - read one from list_bodies

include_static.description: Whether a ray sees static geoms - a geom on a body with no degrees of freedom, such as the ground plane or a wall. Read by both raycast and multi_raycast; false casts against the movable scene only, so a clearance check can ask about dynamic obstacles without the static world answering first

positions.description: Joint name → position mapping for set_joint_positions

hold.description: set_joint_positions: also move the matching position-servo setpoints so the pose survives stepping, instead of being pulled back toward the setpoints the servos already hold (default false, which writes qpos only). A joint driven by a torque or velocity actuator is left alone - its ctrl is not a pose - and so is a joint a tendon couples to one ctrl (every stock gripper), whose ctrl is in tendon units and drives several joints at once. The success text names the joints it left alone.

velocities.description: Joint name → velocity mapping for set_joint_velocities

sensor_name.description: Specific sensor name (or omit for all)

policy_config.description: Provider-specific config dict forwarded to strands_robots.policies.create_policy. Contents depend on policy_provider. For 'groot': host, port, api_token, observation_mapping, action_mapping. For 'lerobot_local': pretrained_name_or_path, policy_type, device, actions_per_step, use_processor, processor_overrides, camera_key_map, obs_rename_override. For 'mock': {} is fine.

stop_when.description: run_policy: optional semantic early-return clause -- the rollout ends as soon as the condition holds in the sim, instead of only when the step budget runs out. Same predicate DSL as a benchmark spec's success: clause: a single bool predicate call like {'predicate': 'grasped', 'body': 'cube', 'gripper_prefix': 'so100'} or {'predicate': 'body_above_z', 'body': 'cube', 'z': 0.2}, or a group {'all': [<call>, ...]} / {'any': [<call>, ...]}. Predicates resolve through the closed registry (never eval/exec); an unknown name or a float-valued reward term is rejected up front with the valid list. Checked after every applied action (also on the async-RTC path, so the stop lands within one control step). Composes with an active recording: frames are captured up to the stop. The result json reports stopped_reason ('predicate'|'budget'|'cancelled'; 'error' on failures) and steps_used so you can decide whether to retry.

cameras.description: List of camera names. Omit to use every camera in the scene. Used by render_all / start_cameras_recording.

output_dir.description: Directory for start_cameras_recording output. Defaults to a platform-appropriate temp directory (tempfile.gettempdir()/strands_robots/recordings).

xml.description: Raw MJCF XML string. Used by replace_scene_mjcf.

ops.description: List of structured MJCF edit ops for action='patch_scene_mjcf'. Each op is a dict like {'op': 'add_body', 'parent': 'world', 'name': 'foo', 'pos': [0,0,1]}, {'op': 'add_geom', 'body': 'foo', 'type': 'sphere', 'size': [0.1]}, {'op': 'add_site', 'body': 'foo', 'name': 'tip', 'pos': [0,0,0.2]}, {'op': 'set_body_pos', 'name': 'foo', 'pos': [1,0,1]}, {'op': 'set_body_quat', 'name': 'foo', 'quat': [1,0,0,0]}, or {'op': 'delete_body', 'name': 'foo'}. Each op accepts only the keys it reads (add_body: parent, name, pos, quat; add_geom: body, type, size, rgba, name, pos, quat; add_site: body, name, pos, size, rgba; set_body_pos: name, pos; set_body_quat: name, quat; delete_body: name) - any other key is rejected, since an unread key would leave the op running on its default (a misspelled 'pos' would move the body to the origin). Numeric fields: 'pos' takes exactly 3 finite components, 'quat' 4, 'rgba' 3 (RGB, completed with an opaque alpha) or 4, and 'size' the count its shape consumes. add_geom's 'type' takes box, capsule, cylinder, ellipsoid, plane or sphere; 'mesh' is refused because this op cannot name a mesh asset - use action='add_object' with shape='mesh' and mesh_path for that. Applied atomically: if any op fails, the whole batch is rolled back.

benchmark_name.description: Name of a registered BenchmarkProtocol (for register_benchmark_from_file / evaluate_benchmark)

spec_path.description: Path to a declarative benchmark spec file (.json, .yaml, .yml). Used by register_benchmark_from_file.

parent.description: Parent body name for attach_bodies/detach_bodies (robot bodies are namespaced '<robot>/<body>'; call list_bodies to discover names)

child.description: Child body name to attach/detach (mode='kinematic' requires it to be a dynamic body with a freejoint)

mode.description: attach_bodies mode: 'weld' adds an equality constraint holding the current relative pose; 'kinematic' teleport-follows the parent every physics step. Neither is a physical grasp.

torquescale.description: attach_bodies weld-only: torque-to-force ratio of the constraint (finite, > 0; default 1.0)

kp.description: actuate_robot position gain: a number applies to every hinge/slide joint; a {joint_name: kp} object actuates only the listed joints. Values must be finite and > 0.

gravity_compensation.description: actuate_robot: apply gravcomp=1 to the robot's bodies (default true)

disable_self_collision.description: actuate_robot: zero contype/conaffinity on ALL the robot's geoms so planner-ignored self-contacts cannot block motion (default false)
